beats.say: Hello! Today we will spot fake pages that pretend to be a robot check.
A page like this gives three steps: press keys, paste a text, confirm.
A real check never asks you to type a command on your keyboard.
The rule: whatever a site tells you to type, do not, and close the page.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs on this check page.

body.text: To continue, complete the steps below:
1. Press the keys on your keyboard that open a window.
2. Paste the copied text into the box.
This check is needed to detect bots.

spots.label: Pressing keys
spots.explain: A real check never asks you to press keyboard keys. This is how a hidden command gets run.

spots.label: Pasting
spots.explain: The text you paste is really a hidden command. Never paste what a site tells you to.

spots.label: The confirm key
spots.explain: When you confirm, the command runs and harmful software is installed. Do not take this step.

spots.label: A fake excuse
spots.explain: Detecting bots is the excuse. A real check asks you to pick pictures or tick a box.

scenes.title: On the forum site
scenes.intro: On a conference site you meet several checks. Choose the right step for each one.

body.text: To continue, press the keys shown and paste the text.

steps.say: The page tells you to press keys and paste.

actions.label: Close the page
actions.feedback: Correct. A check that asks you to type a command is fake, so closing it is the right step.

actions.label: Follow the steps
actions.feedback: The hidden command you pasted installed harmful software. Never follow steps like these.

actions.label: Report to tech support
actions.feedback: Good step. Showing this page to tech support protects your colleagues too.

body.text: To show you are not a robot, select the pictures with traffic lights.

steps.say: This is an ordinary picture check.

actions.label: Select the pictures and confirm
actions.feedback: Correct. This is what a real check looks like: pick pictures or tick a box.

actions.label: Close the page
actions.feedback: That is fine too. If you do not want to continue, you can just close it.

actions.label: Report as an attack
actions.feedback: This check is safe, so there is no need to report it. Only checks that ask for commands are fake.

body.text: The PDF could not be shown. To fix it, copy and run the command below.

steps.say: This page gives you a command to open a document.

actions.label: Close the page
actions.feedback: Correct. A page that says a document will not open is the same trap, so close it.

actions.label: Run the command
actions.feedback: This command installed harmful software on the computer. Do not trust a page that says a document will not open.

actions.label: Report to tech support
actions.feedback: Good choice. Tech support can check the page and warn others.

body.text: To join the meeting, run this command, then refresh the page.

steps.say: Now it says the meeting app has an error.

actions.label: Close the page
actions.feedback: Correct. A meeting app never asks you to run a command, so this is a trap too.

actions.label: Run the command
actions.feedback: The command started harmful software. Any command that claims to fix an error is the same trick.

actions.label: Report to tech support
actions.feedback: Great. Reporting fake error pages like this to tech support helps everyone.

scenes.prompt: Is each check real or a trap?

body.text: Tick the I am not a robot box and continue.

cards.explain: This is an ordinary check. Ticking a box or picking pictures is safe.

body.text: Press the keys that open a window and paste the text.

cards.explain: A check that asks you to type a command is fake. Close the page.

body.text: Type the letters from the picture into the box below.

cards.explain: This is an ordinary check. Typing the letters from a picture starts nothing on your computer.

body.text: Copy this text and paste it into the Run box.

cards.explain: Never run a text a site tells you to copy. It is a hidden command.

question.prompt: What can a real robot check ask of you? Select all that apply.

options.label: Tick a box
options.feedback: Correct. Ticking a box is an ordinary check and it is safe.

options.label: Pick pictures
options.feedback: Correct. Picking pictures is another kind of real check.

options.label: Type the letters from a picture
options.feedback: Correct. Typing letters starts nothing on your computer.

options.label: Press keys and paste a text
options.feedback: This is the trap. A real check never sends you to your computer's own windows.

scenes.explain: A real check stays inside the page. A check that sends you to press keys and paste a text is fake.

points: A real check never asks you to type a command
Never paste a text a site tells you to
Close such a page and report it to tech support
